newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -T-bonds to consolidate, barrier at 112-20.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -T-bonds to consolidate, barrier at 112-20.

text.p: September T-bonds will consolidate on Monday after Friday's spike higher, bumping into trendline resistance at 112-20, technical analysts said.
Consistently strong buying power will continue to underpin the market with support at 111-26 seen holding, they added.

"There's evidence of consistent buying power in Treasuries but I'd be fairly cautious as the market is up against a sloping resistance line," said Elli Gifford, an independent technical analyst near Cambridge.
She put resistance at 112-20 then 113-00. If the market does break through there, the February 18 high at 113-09 would act as a barrier, Gifford added.
By 0856 GMT, September T-bonds were down 3/32 at 112-14 after breaking through resistance on Friday to reach 112-24. The 14-day RSI was at 71.5 percent.
Gerry Celaya, senior technical analyst at American Express Bank in London expected the market to consolidate its sharp gains.

"It's hard to get bearish right now but Friday's session could have been pretty significant. We had a high of 112-24 and we didn't follow up too much on it," he said. "So I guess it's looking for some consolidation."
On the upside he put critical resistance at 112-24, followed by 113-09 then 114-00.

On the downside, Gifford said the market would find a band of support at 112-08, the June 18 high, to 111-26, the June 19 low. "Despite the fact it is marginally overbought, I suspect that will hold," she said.
Celaya also put support at 111-26, then 111-17 -- a double low from last week. Below there, although unlikely, support would come in at 111-08/09, lows in mid-June, he said.
